content.text:
**Finding: deviation (critical) — § 21.1 cap basis.**

The liability section looks compliant at first glance — the cap is expressly mutual, indirect/consequential damages are mutually excluded, restoration/notice/incident-response costs are confirmed as direct damages, and § 21.3 "Excluded Claims" tracks our preferred carve-out list (confidentiality, data protection, security, indemnification, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud, IP infringement), with Customer's payment obligations expressly not treated as damages.

The problem is the cap measure. § 21.1 caps liability at "the **Fees** paid or payable by Customer under **the first Order Form**", and § 1.5 defines "Fees" as the Implementation Fee, which § 1.6 fixes as a one-time **USD 12,000** charge. So both parties' aggregate liability is effectively ceilinged at ~USD 12,000 regardless of actual spend — an illusory cap well below the 6-months'-fees walk-away threshold, and in practice most protective of Vendor.

Redline (validated, ok:true) makes the smallest possible change to § 21.1:

> ...shall not exceed the ~~Fees~~ **greater of (a) all amounts** paid or payable by Customer under ~~the first Order Form~~ **this Agreement** during the twelve months preceding the event giving rise to the claim **and (b) USD 1,000,000**.

Mutuality, the exclusions in § 21.2 and the Excluded Claims definition are left untouched. Fallback if Vendor resists the USD 1,000,000 floor: accept a straight twelve months' amounts paid or payable basis.
